data.question: What controls and deadlines now determine whether and how Columbus continues Flock-linked surveillance after the Aug. 10 hearing?
data.method: Recursive review of official Columbus legislation and records plus reputable local reporting.
data.scope: Flock contract term, ForceMetrics amendment, retention, sharing controls, policy status, and decision deadlines.
findings: Ordinance 3181-2024 authorized $228,000 for 38 fixed Flock LPRs under a two-year term beginning when the purchase order is confirmed or certified.
Axios reports the current Flock contract reaches a renewal-or-lapse decision point in December 2026.
Ordinance 1510-2025 added ForceMetrics to the existing Flock agreement for a free one-year non-renewable trial; published continuation pricing begins at $209,999 for year two.
Columbus Records Commission materials list Flock LPR data retention at 30 days, compared with 30 months for Axon and Vigilant LPR data.
WOSU reported CPD disabled nationwide Flock sharing in June 2026 and Mayor Ginther ordered statewide sharing stopped in July after the audit.
As of June 25, WOSU reported CPD was still developing a Flock-specific policy.
conclusions: The highest-value next records are the exact contract clock, renewal procurement or legislation, final CPD policy, current one-to-one sharing allowlist, and ForceMetrics trial disposition.
limitations: No official post-hearing vote or renewal filing was identified in this pass.
